claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the current record because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and documented monitoring/model-card controls are sufficient despite an unresolved segment-level evaluation gap.
decision_criteria: If admissible records show the affected segment is a named contractual or launch segment and no approved risk acceptance or required disclosure exists, certification is not adequately supported.
If admissible records show approved risk acceptance or completed required disclosure covering the unresolved gap before launch, the verdict could improve.
Public guidance on monitoring and documentation is secondary; the decision turns on whether the internal materiality and disclosure predicates are actually satisfied.
Because only an actor summary is available, unsupported predicates should remain unresolved rather than presumed satisfied.
evidence_requests: The underlying product materiality note supporting the 6% projected first-month traffic claim.
The source record showing the small-business onboarding segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, including contract or commitment language.
The open legal review record and its current status on whether disclosure is required.
The exact release policy artifact requiring disclosure of material limitations and any exception path.
Any approved risk acceptance covering this unresolved segment-level gap before launch.
The draft or final model-card/disclosure text proposed for this limitation, if certification depends on disclosure rather than remediation.
specific_concerns: The controlling policy text says materiality is triggered when a weakness affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; the packet itself says the affected segment is named in two paid pilot commitments.
The Actor relies on a 'non-core' 6% traffic label, but the policy expressly says low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality in this circumstance.
Legal review on disclosure remains open, which the policy identifies as a reason materiality is not resolved.
The packet does not show that the limitation was resolved before launch or covered by an approved risk acceptance, even though the cited release policy requires one of those conditions.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not by themselves answer the disclosure/materiality predicate.
Evidence access is limited to the Actor's summary, so key predicates cannot be independently verified from admissible source records.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record.
That the 6% projected traffic share is sufficient to treat the weakness as non-material.
That monitoring and model-card documentation alone satisfy the release policy without proof of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that public governance guidance overrides or satisfies the specific internal materiality/disclosure rule.
